description: The Scottish House Condition Survey is the largest housing research project in Scotland and the only national survey that inspects the physical condition of homes as well as interviewing householders. It is run by the Scottish Government, earlier by Communities Scotland and Scottish Homes, and is now an integrated part of the Scottish Household Survey, with fieldwork each year from January to December; its statistics were designated National Statistics in 2010 and reconfirmed in 2020. It monitors stock condition over time, provides a benchmark for local surveys and an information resource for housing policy; outputs include key findings reports, local authority tables and a dashboard on damp, mould and condensation. Coverage: a national sample of dwellings across Scotland. Access: reports and tables on gov.scot; microdata such as the 2002 survey through the UK Data Service for registered users. Licence: microdata under the UK Data Service End User Licence; published outputs free. Caveats: a sample survey, so local estimates carry wide uncertainty. Simulation uses: stock condition and damp inputs for housing retrofit and heat or cold risk models. Related records: the English Housing Survey and the GB National Energy Efficiency Data-Framework.
